messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: suggestions for enhancing print
parts:
Hi,

I have been doing a lot of debugging by printf lately. Since this is the
only practical way to debug models that I know of, I think that making
it a bit more convenient (= less typing) would be a huge
improvement. The two proposals below reflect the way I usually debug
code, which may not be universal, but still this could be a starting
point for a discussion (I checked the issues and could not find anything
similar, sorry if I missed something).

1. Printing arguments to the print call

Instead of writing

print("i = ", i, ", x[i] = ", x[i], ", y[i] = ", y[i]);

there could be a function printvars which would be called as

printvars(i, x[i], y[i]);

This would print its arguments, too, followed by values, separated by
commas. In Lisp-like languages one would implement printvars as a macro,
since it needs to see the variable names it was called with, and I don't
know if the parser of Stan retains this information.

When printvars encounters a literal string, it could just print that as
is, eg

printvars("debugging inner loop", i, x[i], y[i]);

would be equivalent to

print("debugging inner loop", "i = ", i, ", x[i] = ", x[i], ", y[i] = ", y[i]);

2. Interpolating, similar to printf. I guess there is no need to
explain. Would extend current print in an upward-compatible way (except
if one uses % in strings).

3. Interpolating version of printvars: literal strings that have
formatting directives would just gobble as many of the following
arguments as needed, but otherwise it would work as printvars.

(2) and (3) are wishlist items, I understand that the Stan developers
are busy with a lot of other things, but just plain vanilla printvars
(1) would make debugging a lot easier.

Best,

Tamas
